questions.q: Which of following best describes the role of a central bank acting as the lender of last resort?
options: Providing long-term equity funding to private startup corporation during a recession
Guaranteeing personal retail bank accounts against identity theft and digital fraud
Providing emergency credit to solvent commercial banks facing acute temporary liquidity shortages
Buying nonperforming corporate bonds directly from retail individuals’ investors.

questions.q: What is the core operational difference between NEFT and RTGS?
options: NEFT settles transactions in batches at specific times, whereas RTGS processes transactions individually and in real time.
RTGS is exclusively meant for international cross border trade while NEFT handles domestic cash
NEFT has a mandatory high minimum transaction limit whereas RTGS has no minimum limit
RTGS can only be used on weekends whereas NEFT works only on weekends.
questions.explain: As per the official answer key, the answer to Q294 is A) NEFT settles transactions in batches at specific times, whereas RTGS processes transactions individually and in real time..

questions.q: How will a commercial bank calculate NIM?
options: Net interest income divided by average earning assets
Total interest earned divided by total assets
Net income divided by shareholders equity
Non interest income divided by operating expenses.

questions.q: Using DuPont analysis, if a banks return on assets (ROA) remains constant while its financial leverage multiplier (asset/ equity) increases. What will happen to its return on equity?
questions.explain: As per the official answer key, the answer to Q297 is C) ROE will increase.

questions.q: A persistent very high loan to deposit ratio – say exceeding 100% generally signals what type of primary vulnerability for a bank?
options: Excess uninvest cash reserves sitting idle in the vault.
High operational efficiency and low administrative overhead
Over reliance on low cost savings deposit
Potential liquidity risk requiring the bank to source higher cost wholesale or interbank funding
questions.explain: As per the official answer key, the answer to Q298 is D) Potential liquidity risk requiring the bank to source higher cost wholesale or interbank funding.

questions.q: How will be banks efficiency ratio conventionally defined, and what does a lower percentage indicate?
options: Non-interest expenses divided by revenue a lower percentage indicates higher operational efficiency.
Total credit losses divided by total loans a lower percentage means worse credit quality
Interest paid divided by interest earned a lower percentage means poor deposit acquisition
Operating income divided by total assets, a lower percentage means stronger performance.
questions.explain: As per the official answer key, the answer to Q299 is A) Non-interest expenses divided by revenue a lower percentage indicates higher operational efficiency..

questions.q: What does a provision coverage ratios (PCR) of 100% signify for a banking institution?
options: The bank has covered 100% of its total performing loan portfolio against market risk
The bank has zero bad loans and full compliance with cash reserve caps
The bank has set aside provisions equal to the total value of its impaired or non- performing loans
The bank has leveraged its equity 100-fold relative to Tier 1 capital.
questions.explain: As per the official answer key, the answer to Q300 is C) The bank has set aside provisions equal to the total value of its impaired or non- performing loans.
